_doc: Procedural copywriter grammar (src/core/copy.gd). '#sym#' expands a random alternative; '#sym.cap#' capitalises, '#sym.upper#' upper-cases, '#sym.a#' adds a/an. '{planet}', '{player}', '{faction}' are filled by the caller. Entry points used by the game: ad_body/headline (billboards), slogan (holograms), <venue>_name (shop signs), street, news (HUD ticker), flyer + graffiti (wall details), floor_notice, pa (public announcements), menu (stall boards), chatter (NPC small talk). Add alternatives freely.

food_scene: Steam rolls off a wok the size of a satellite dish.
A plastic stool, a flickering menu and a smell you'd sell your air for.
Rain drums on the awning. Inside it's warm and loud and smells of garlic.
Three regulars hunch over their bowls without looking up. A good sign. Or a hostage situation.
The menu board flickers between #dish# and something with no name.
A cat sleeps on the counter. There's a cat on the menu board too. Different cat, hopefully.
food_keeper: The cook doesn't look up. "#dish#? Or #dish#? Those are the choices."
"Sit, sit! Today's special is #dish#. Yesterday's special was also #dish#."
"Cash, credits or a good story. Mostly credits."
The owner taps a sign: NO PASTE-SHAMING. "What'll it be?"
"You look hungry. Everyone looks hungry. Sit down."
"Kitchen closes when the rain stops. The rain never stops."
bar_scene: Synth-pop on a busted speaker. The floor is sticky in a reassuring way.
A neon sign buzzes 'OPEN' with the P burned out.
Somebody in the corner is losing an argument with a jukebox.
Two dockers arm-wrestle under a dead hologram of a cocktail.
The air in here is thick, warm and almost certainly unbilled.
A screen over the bar plays #media_product# on mute. Nobody watches.
bar_keeper: The bartender slides you a coaster. It's an ad for #product#.
"What'll it be? And don't say water. Water's extra."
"First drink's full price. Second drink's full price. I don't do discounts."
"If you're with #faction#, you pay double. If you're not, you pay regular double."
The bartender polishes a glass that will never be clean. "Talk or drink. Or both."
"House special tonight: liquid air on the rocks. Rocks are extra."
karaoke_scene: Somebody in booth 3 is murdering a love song with real commitment.
A disco ball with half its mirrors missing throws light around like loose change.
The song list scrolls past: three centuries of pirated heartbreak.
Six dock workers scream a power ballad in perfect harmony.
The mic smells of mint and regret.
karaoke_keeper: "Booths are by the hour. Talent not included."
"Tonight's hit is '#song#' by #band#. Everyone's sick of it. Everyone sings it."
"Sing something sad. The sad ones get tips."
"The machine scores you. It's never given anyone more than a 6. It's owned by #faction#."
arcade_scene: Cabinets from four centuries blink in the dark, all of them playing to nobody.
A kid with no shoes holds the top score on every machine.
The carpet has seen things. Glowing, beeping things.
A claw machine full of air canisters. Nobody has ever won one.
arcade_keeper: "Tokens! Five for #small_num# credits! Or one for a face scan!"
The attendant points at a cabinet called #cabinet#. "New one. Nobody's beaten level 2."
"No crying on the machines. They short out."
"High score gets a free air canister. High score is 9,999,999. Good luck."
clinic_scene: The waiting room is full. Everyone's holding a number and a coupon.
A cracked green cross flickers. The chairs are bolted down. So are the magazines.
A poster asks: IS YOUR PAIN COVERED? Underneath, smaller: (IT IS NOT).
Something beeps steadily in the back room. Either a machine or a very calm patient.
clinic_keeper: The medic looks at you, then at your wallet. "Where does it hurt? Be specific, it's itemised."
"No insurance? Good. Insurance just makes it slower."
"I can fix most things. I can't fix the price."
A nurse-drone chirps: "WELCOME. YOUR WAIT TIME IS #small_num# HOURS. OR #small_num# CREDITS."
pawn_scene: Shelves of somebody's whole life, priced by the kilo.
A wedding ring, a prosthetic hand and a signed photo of a news anchor share one display case.
Behind the counter: WE BUY ANYTHING. WE SELL IT BACK FOR MORE.
A stuffed real bird watches you from a high shelf. The price tag just says 'ASK'.
pawn_keeper: "Buying or selling? Either way, I win. Nothing personal."
"Everything's got a price. Even you. Especially you."
"No questions asked. Lots of answers given, though."
"Don't touch the cursed stuff. It's on the left. Or the right. I forget."
motel_scene: Sleep pods stacked eight high, humming like a fridge full of dreams.
The lobby has one plant. It's plastic. It's dying anyway.
A sign: ROOMS BY THE HOUR, BY THE NIGHT, OR BY THE DEBT.
Somewhere above, a pod alarm plays the #brand# jingle.
motel_keeper: The clerk doesn't look up from #media_product#. "Pod or premium pod? Premium has a window. It's painted on."
"Checkout is at #time#. Late checkout is billed per snore."
"Dreams are recorded for quality purposes. Opting out is #small_num# credits."
loans_scene: A smiling hologram greets you by your credit score.
Gold carpet, white leather and no windows at all.
A brochure shows a happy family. The small print says they belong to Halcyon.
Every chair faces a screen counting up somebody's interest.
loans_keeper: "Debt is just a future you haven't paid for yet!"
"Collateral? Your lungs will do. Most people have two."
The broker's smile doesn't move. "Let's talk about your potential."
tattoo_scene: Needles buzz like angry bees. Flash sheets cover every wall.
The artist's arms are a gallery. One tattoo is a barcode. It still scans.
A customer winces in the chair, getting a #brand# logo. Sponsored ink pays the rent.
Neon light, antiseptic and an old synth record crackling.
tattoo_keeper: "What'll it be? No corporate logos. Unless you're paying corporate prices."
"I can cover a debt barcode. It'll cost you, though."
tapes_scene: Walls of cassettes. Real ones. Every label hand-written.
A tape deck plays something with real drums. It sounds illegal.
A crate marked BANNED BY LUMEN - 3 FOR 2.
Dust, magnetic tape and a cat asleep on the #genre# section.
tapes_keeper: The shopkeeper hums along to #band#. "You into #genre#? Course you are."
"No streaming in here. Streaming is how they find you."
"That one's a bootleg of #media_product#, uncut. Don't tell anyone."
air_scene: Canisters stacked like ammunition, every one labelled MOUNTAIN FRESH.
A pressure gauge ticks. The queue breathes shallowly, saving up.
The kiosk hisses. It might be a leak. It might be the ambience.
air_keeper: "Fresh air! Bottled today! Or yesterday! Or the day before!"
The vendor taps a canister. "Smell that? That's freedom. #small_num# credits."
implants_scene: Robot arms twitch on hooks. A box of eyes sits by the register.
Sparks rain off a workbench where someone is getting a new knee.
The diagnostics screen flickers: WARRANTY VOID.
A poster of a smiling cyborg: UPGRADE OR BE UPGRADED.
implants_keeper: "Let's see what we're working with." The mechanic squints at you like a used car.
fortune_scene: Incense, a cracked crystal ball and a card reader.
Beaded curtains and a cat with one eye. The eye is a camera.
Tarot cards on the table, every one of them sponsored.
A neon palm glows in the window: YOUR FUTURE, SUBSCRIPTION-FREE.
fortune_keeper: "I see... debt. No, wait. That's everyone."
"Cross my palm with credits and I'll cross yours with destiny."
"The stars say #weather.lower#. The stars are sponsored."
corp_store_scene: Bright, clean, scentless. Music designed to make you forget you have a home.
Every shelf faces you. Every product smiles.
A greeter-drone sings the store's name in four-part harmony.
The aisles are arranged so the exit is always one more aisle away.
corp_store_keeper: "WELCOME, VALUED CUSTOMER. YOU ARE BEING VALUED."
An associate smiles with every tooth. "Have you considered upgrading your loyalty tier?"
